evidence.slot: tilt the teapot to pour into the mug.path.trans[1]

rounds.diagnosis: The pour stage's path pinned the spout height into the same narrow band as its subgoal (+8 to +10 cm above the mug opening), but the stage starts where the carry stage ends, with the spout only a few centimetres above the rim — roughly 3.8 cm below the path band, far more than the planner's start projection can absorb. Since path terms must hold from entry to subgoal, no motion could ever enter the region. Freeing the height row on the pour path lets the teapot rise from the carry standoff to the pouring height while the centring row keeps the spout over the mug opening; the subgoal still enforces the large standoff and the tipped spout orientation, so the pour itself is unchanged.
